title: Meet TVL (Total Value Locked)
objectives: Understand what Total Value Locked (TVL) measures across pools and protocols
Identify why TVL can mislead users through double counting and circular backing
Evaluate real protocol liquidity depth vs superficial headline TVL

steps.title: What Total Value Locked (TVL) Means
steps.body:
**Total Value Locked (TVL)** is the aggregate dollar value of all cryptocurrency assets currently deposited in a decentralized finance protocol's smart contracts. Add up everything sitting in the vaults and you get one headline number.

Investors track TVL on analytics dashboards like DeFiLlama because it serves as a rough proxy for three things:
- **Trust:** how much real capital users are willing to park in the protocol.
- **Usage:** how actively the protocol is actually being used, not just talked about.
- **Liquidity depth:** how much value is available for trading, lending, or borrowing.

But a big number is not automatically a healthy one. TVL is easy to inflate, double-count, and misrepresent - which is exactly what the next section covers.

steps.title: Why TVL Can Mislead You
steps.body:
While TVL is widely cited, it has major traps:

1. **Double Counting:** If you deposit 10 SOL into Marinade to get mSOL, and then deposit that mSOL into Kamino as lending collateral, the same $1,500 of capital gets counted twice in aggregate stats!
2. **Inflated Token Valuations:** If a protocol locks 1 billion of its own illiquid governance tokens priced at $1 each on paper, headline TVL might say $1 Billion, even though selling $5,000 would crash the token to zero.
3. **Mercenary Capital:** Yield-farming mercenaries can deposit $50M for 3 days to harvest tokens and withdraw everything immediately.

steps.title: Under the Hood: How DefiLlama Computes TVL
steps.body: TVL adapters query on-chain token account balances for each smart contract vault: `TVL = Σ (token_balance × spot_price)`. Reputable aggregators explicitly provide toggles to exclude double counting, staked governance tokens, and borrowed debt so users see genuine backing liquidity.

questions.prompt: How can a protocol artificially inflate its TVL without having real user deposits?
options: By setting up an RPC node
By minting billions of unbacked tokens with no market liquidity and locking them in its own contracts
By deploying on Solana instead of Ethereum
By verifying contract code on an explorer
questions.explainRight: Correct! Paper valuations on illiquid self-minted tokens can create illusionary TVL.
questions.explainWrong: Incorrect. Illiquid self-minted tokens locked in vaults are the classic method used to inflate superficial TVL.

questions.prompt: What is 'double counting' in DeFi TVL metrics?
options: Counting the same underlying capital multiple times as it moves through recursive yield and lending layers
questions.explainRight: Spot on! When wrapped or yield-bearing tokens are deposited into subsequent protocols, the same dollars can be counted repeatedly.
questions.explainWrong: Incorrect. Double counting refers to capital that is deposited into one protocol, converted to a derivative, and deposited into another.
